<u>Yehicle Mortality</u>
X X
Ford Motor Company. Ford believes NHTSA should use actual vehicle mortality figures for NPA's rather than assume a ten-year vehicle life.
disagreed with NHTSA assumptions on vehicle miles traveled (VMT) and average vehicle life. They cited a cursory reference search that indicated annual mileage in excess of 14,000 miles and average truck age of 6.94 years versus 5.99 years for passenger cars. They also cited a reference which reported that 15.3 percent of passenger vehicles on the road in 1975 were over 10 years of age, and 25.7 percent of pickup trucks on the road in 1972 were over 10 years of age. UM also commented that the apparently weak assumptions result in misleading information being given to the public.
Summary. Ford stated that NHTSA should use actual mortality figures for NPA's rather than assume a ten-year life. UM stated that they disagreed with NHTSA's truck mileage statistics.
